Existing Bloch constructors, certificates and rational/integral/modulo comparisons are reused by id. Regulator agreement belongs to P.2 and D.2. V.6 is planned with explicit computational and normalization gaps, not closed.

nodes.title: Integral root-of-unity multiple
nodes.statement: Let F be a field, ζ a primitive m-th root with m≥2, P(F) the pre-Bloch group and ∂ its boundary to Suslin’s antisymmetric square. Define rootMultiple(ζ,m)=(m[ζ], h_m) in B(F)=ker ∂, where h_m is the boundary vanishing supplied by V.6/root-of-unity-symbol. The reusable construction takes any abelian groups P,W, homomorphism δ:P→W, x∈P, natural m and proof δ(mx)=0, and returns (mx,h)∈ker δ. The proof is not data on which the resulting element depends. Exact order is needed only for the field specialization, not the generic kernel construction.
hypotheses: F is a field, m≥2 and IsPrimitiveRoot ζ m for the field specialization; hence ζ≠0,1.
Use the antisymmetric quotient, retaining diagonal two-torsion, throughout the integral construction.
proofSteps: Import the actual boundary formula and m∂[ζ]=0 from V.6/root-of-unity-symbol; bilinearity turns the first factor ζ^m into 1.
Insert m[ζ] into the kernel using V.3/bloch-group. Equality and change of annihilating multiple follow from equality of underlying elements and proof irrelevance.
Under a field map transport the symbol and the boundary; kernel functoriality gives the stated compatibility.

sources.match: The cyclotomic paragraph motivates the integral multiple; the stronger antisymmetric boundary calculation is imported from the reviewed parent, rather than inferred from the exterior-square calculation.

acceptance: For a primitive sixth root ω over ℚ(√−3), 6[ω] is accepted although [ω] is rejected by the diagonal obstruction.
Over a field where −1 is a square, the same construction agrees with six times the integral raw class of ω.

uses.how: The K₃ classes corresponding to D[ζ_D] supply circular-unit inputs.
Transport integral input to coefficient rings in which the root order is invertible.
Provides the honest integral numerator before division by a unit.

api.name: rootMultiple
api.statement: For δ,x,m,h:δ(mx)=0, return the kernel element with underlying value mx.

api.name: rootMultiple_coe
api.statement: The inclusion of rootMultiple(δ,x,m,h) into P is mx.

api.name: rootMultiple_proof_irrel
api.statement: For two proofs h,h′ of δ(mx)=0, the resulting kernel elements are equal.

api.name: rootMultiple_zero
api.statement: rootMultiple(δ,0,m,h)=0; rootMultiple(δ,x,0,h)=0.

api.name: rootMultiple_of_mem
api.statement: If b∈ker δ has underlying x, rootMultiple(δ,x,m,h)=mb.

api.name: rootMultiple_mul
api.statement: If δ(mx)=0 and δ((mk)x)=0, rootMultiple at mk is k times rootMultiple at m.

api.name: rootMultiple_map
api.statement: For f:P→P′ and g:W→W′ with δ′f=gδ, the induced kernel map sends rootMultiple(δ,x,m,h) to rootMultiple(δ′,f(x),m,h′).

tests.name: rootMultiple_mod_two
tests.statement: For δ:ℤ→ℤ/2 reduction, x=1 and m=2, the underlying rootMultiple is 2, not 1.

tests.name: rootMultiple_zero_multiplier
tests.statement: For every δ and x, the kernel element built with annihilator 0 is zero.

tests.name: rootMultiple_kernel_compat
tests.statement: For b in the Mathlib additive kernel of δ and m=3, rootMultiple built from the underlying b equals 3b in that kernel.

tests.name: rootMultiple_raw_rejected
tests.statement: For δ:ℤ→ℤ/2 reduction, 1 is not in ker δ although 2 is. A constructor returning the raw symbol fails this test.

nodes.title: Root-of-unity class over a coefficient ring
nodes.statement: Let δ:P→W be an additive homomorphism of abelian groups, B=ker δ, x∈P, m∈ℕ, and h:δ(mx)=0. Let R be a commutative ring and u∈R× with underlying value the image of m. Define rootCoefficient(δ,x,m,h,u)=(mx,h)⊗u⁻¹ in B⊗_ℤ R. Its image under B⊗R→P⊗R is x⊗1. This construction, without any flatness assumption, specializes for x=[ζ] to the parent’s rootClassMod (R=ℤ/n, gcd(m,n)=1), rootClassLoc (R=ℤ[1/m]) and rootClassPadic (R=ℤ_p, p∤m). It does not assert that tensoring the kernel identifies it with the kernel of the reduced boundary.
hypotheses: δ(mx)=0, R commutative and u a unit whose value is m in R.
For the field specialization ζ has exact order m≥2. Coprimality or localization supplies the unit; when m is not invertible no raw coefficient class is constructed by this recipe.
proofSteps: Use the integral kernel element from integral-root-multiple and the canonical Mathlib tensor product; take its pure tensor with u⁻¹.
Apply the tensor of the kernel inclusion. The ℤ-balancing relation and uu⁻¹=1 give x⊗1.
For two annihilators m,l with invertible images, the equality l(mx,h_m)=m(lx,h_l) inside B proves equality of the two divided tensors. No injectivity after tensoring is used.

Tensor functoriality gives field maps and change of coefficient ring. Compare the three specializations with the already planned V.6/root-of-unity-class, including the standard B⊗ℤ/n≅B/n identification exported there.

sources.match: Invertibility of the root order is the coefficient hypothesis. The generic unit-division API is derived by tensor balancing, not attributed as a separate CGZ theorem.

acceptance: Modulo n requires gcd(m,n)=1; p-adic coefficients require p∤m.
Over ℚ(√−3) and n=5 the class for a sixth root is defined even though the raw integral symbol is not in B.
For a nonflat coefficient ring the inclusion of B⊗R into P⊗R can have a kernel; projection to the raw tensor does not imply uniqueness of arbitrary lifts.

uses.how: A single general construction reconciles its three existing specializations without replanning them.
Provides the class in B⊗ℤ_p when the root order is prime to p, retaining the integral numerator.
Provides quotient input for finite Chern maps; this input lies in B/n before entering the étale Bloch group.

api.name: rootCoefficient
api.statement: The pure tensor rootMultiple(δ,x,m,h)⊗u⁻¹ in B⊗R, for the specified unit u.

api.name: rootCoefficient_toPre
api.statement: Under the tensor of the kernel inclusion, rootCoefficient maps to x⊗1.

api.name: rootCoefficient_zero
api.statement: For x=0 and any valid denominator, rootCoefficient=0.

api.name: rootCoefficient_of_mem
api.statement: If b∈B has underlying x, rootCoefficient=b⊗1.

api.name: rootCoefficient_denominator_independent
api.statement: For two annihilating positive or zero natural numbers m,l with invertible images u,v in R, the divided tensor classes coincide.

api.name: rootCoefficient_changeRing
api.statement: For a ring map ρ:R→S, tensoring id_B with ρ sends the class to the class with unit ρ(u).

api.name: rootCoefficient_map
api.statement: For a commuting boundary square f:P→P′,g:W→W′, tensoring its kernel map with id_R sends the class at x to that at f(x).

api.name: rootCoefficient_specializations
api.statement: Under B⊗ℤ/n≅B/n this is rootClassMod; for ℤ[1/m] it is rootClassLoc; for ℤ_p with p∤m it is rootClassPadic, with the parent’s conventions.

tests.name: rootCoefficient_mod_five
tests.statement: For δ:ℤ→ℤ/2 reduction, x=1,m=2,R=ℤ/5 and u=2, the image in ℤ⊗ℤ/5 is 1⊗1 and the defining tensor in B⊗ℤ/5 is (2,h)⊗3.

tests.name: rootCoefficient_zero_test
tests.statement: The class at x=0 equals zero for every unit denominator.

tests.name: rootCoefficient_two_denominators
tests.statement: For δ:ℤ→ℤ/2 reduction, x=1,R=ℤ/5, the classes using annihilators 2 and 4 coincide; they both agree with pure tensor division in Mathlib.

tests.name: rootCoefficient_nonflat
tests.statement: For δ:ℤ→ℤ/2 reduction and R=ℤ/2, there is a nonzero tensor in (ker δ)⊗R whose image in ℤ⊗R is zero. Thus projection to the raw tensor does not characterize an arbitrary class and 2 cannot be used as a unit denominator in this R.

nodes.title: Fibre of the integral Suslin comparison
nodes.statement: For an infinite field F write the imported exact sequence as 0→T(F) --i→ K₃^ind(F) --q→ B(F)→0, with T(F) the enhanced Tor term in the parent. For β∈B(F), define SuslinLift(q,β)={k∈K₃^ind(F) | q(k)=β}. It is a nonempty fibre; T acts freely and transitively by k↦k+i(t). This is a torsor of witnesses, without a distinguished origin. For the generic API, q:K→B and i:T→K are homomorphisms of abelian groups, q surjective, i injective, and im i=ker q. The fibre definition itself needs only q and β.
hypotheses: F infinite for the source cited here; the parent’s separately justified finite-field comparisons are reused in their own ranges.
The torsor statements use exactness, including the enhanced two-primary extension, not ordinary Tor or a chosen direct sum decomposition.
proofSteps: Define the subtype fibre using the actual q of V.6/comparison-integral.
Use its surjectivity for nonemptiness. Exactness says the difference of two representatives is i(t); injectivity of i gives the unique t.
Translation and its laws use the additive group structure. A field map induces a fibre map by naturality of the parent comparison.
The generic finite-group example uses the actual Mathlib reduction ℤ/24→ℤ/6 and detects the nonsplit extension.

sources.match: The imported Suslin exact sequence supplies the fibre, nonemptiness and precisely its enhanced-Tor ambiguity.

acceptance: For β=0, zero is a witness but other kernel elements can be witnesses.
For F=ℚ the parent’s nonsplit ℤ/4→ℤ/24→ℤ/6 model gives four witnesses over each β. It cannot be replaced with ℤ/6⊕ℤ/4.

uses.how: Makes the ambiguity of a chosen K₃^ind preimage explicit; passage to Quillen K₃ has the additional Milnor ambiguity.
An explicit Bloch numerator can be paired with a K₃ representative while preserving what is and is not canonical.

api.name: SuslinLift
api.statement: The fibre subtype of q at β.

api.name: SuslinLift.ofRep
api.statement: Given k and q(k)=β, produce a witness.

api.name: SuslinLift.over
api.statement: Every witness has q(value)=β.

api.name: SuslinLift.ext
api.statement: Two witnesses are equal iff their underlying K-elements are equal.

api.name: SuslinLift.choose
api.statement: Surjectivity of q provides a noncomputable witness for each β; no additivity or naturality of choose is asserted.

api.name: SuslinLift.translate
api.statement: For t∈T and q∘i=0, translate k by i(t) within the same fibre.

api.name: SuslinLift.translate_zero_add
api.statement: Translation by 0 is the identity and successive translations by t and s equal translation by s+t.

api.name: SuslinLift.unique_difference
api.statement: When i is injective and im i=ker q, for witnesses a,b there is a unique t∈T with b.value=a.value+i(t).

api.name: SuslinLift.map
api.statement: For f:K→K′,g:B→B′ with q′f=gq, map a witness above β to the witness with representative f(k) above g(β).

api.name: SuslinLift.map_id_comp
api.statement: The fibre maps respect identity maps and composition of commuting squares.

tests.name: SuslinLift_zero_test
tests.statement: For every additive q, 0 with q(0)=0 is an element of SuslinLift(q,0).

tests.name: SuslinLift_Q_fibre
tests.statement: For q:ℤ/24→ℤ/6 reduction, the fibre over 1 has cardinality 4 and underlying representatives 1,7,13,19.

tests.name: SuslinLift_kernel_compat
tests.statement: For β=0 and q:K→B, the underlying representatives are exactly Mathlib’s additive kernel q.ker.

tests.name: SuslinLift_Q_nonsplit
tests.statement: The reduction ℤ/24→ℤ/6 has no additive section. Fibre nonemptiness cannot justify an additive canonical choice of lifts.

nodes.title: Certified finite bar-cycle lift
nodes.statement: Let F be infinite, G=St(F) the imported stable Steinberg group, A the trivial integral representation, and ψ:H₃(G,ℤ)→B(F) the composite H₃(St(F),ℤ)≅K₃(F)→K₃^ind(F)→B(F). For β∈B(F), define BarLiftCertificate(ψ,β)={z∈Z₃(G,ℤ) | ψ(π(z))=β}. Here Z₃ and π are Mathlib’s cycles and their projection to homology. The underlying chain is a finitely supported integral function on triples (equivalently Fin 3→G), with bar boundary [g|h|k]↦[h|k]−[gh|k]+[g|hk]−[g|h]. Its data are a finite chain, proof its boundary vanishes, and proof its homology image is β. This does not include an algorithm producing a chain from a five-term certificate.
hypotheses: The field-specific ψ and its surjectivity come from the parent’s V.1 and V.6 nodes. The witness type itself is defined for any group G and supplied ψ to any abelian B.
Use the unnormalized inhomogeneous bar complex with trivial integral coefficients. A proof that a pre-Bloch symbol combination has boundary zero and a bar cycle are different kinds of certificate.
proofSteps: Import V.1/bar-cycle-model and k3-h3-steinberg, and compose their homology identification with the integral Suslin comparison and K₃→K₃^ind.
Use the existing Mathlib cycle type and π; define the subtype imposing ψπ(z)=β. Its chain inclusion is finite support and carries the required cycle equation.
A supplied finite chain and both proofs construct a witness. Adding a degree-four boundary leaves its homology class, hence its certified Bloch target, unchanged.
The parent’s existential certificate-to-bar-cycle theorem and the surjectivity of cycles→homology yield a noncomputable chosen witness. They give no bounded or executable synthesis procedure.
Map along a group/field homomorphism using the imported bar functor and a commuting ψ square; identity and composition follow from the supplied maps.

sources.locator: VI.5.12, p29, together with the parent’s V.1 homological model
sources.match: The surjectivity passage supports existence; it does not produce a chain from finite five-term data.

sources.locator: §2.1, bar resolution and its differential, p2
sources.match: Pins the bar sign convention; trivial coefficients remove the distinction between its right-module and Mathlib’s left-representation leading action.

acceptance: The zero chain certifies β=0. A noncycle cannot be certified merely because an informal symbolic expression evaluates to a Bloch element.

Adding a four-boundary changes the chain while preserving its homology image. Two witnesses over β need not have equal homology classes; their Quillen K₃ representatives differ by ker(K₃→B), including Milnor and enhanced-Tor contributions.
The computational synthesis gap remains explicitly recorded.

uses.how: Turns the existence statement into a reusable witness interface without confusing it with an algorithm.

uses.where: V.6/five-term-certificate and certificate-soundness in the reviewed parent
uses.how: An equality certificate identifies the target β, after which an independently supplied bar lift can be transported across that equality.
Converts the certified homology class into an actual Quillen K₃ representative, retaining the full ambiguity.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate
api.statement: The subtype of actual degree-three cycles z with ψπ(z)=β.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.chain
api.statement: Include the witness cycle into Mathlib’s finite-support chain module.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.cycle_eq
api.statement: The differential of chain(c) is zero.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.homology
api.statement: The homology representative is π(cycle(c)) in the imported H₃.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.over
api.statement: ψ(homology(c))=β.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.ofCycle
api.statement: Given z∈Z₃ and ψπ(z)=β, construct the witness; the standard cyclesMk constructor accepts a finite chain and its zero-boundary proof.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.ext
api.statement: Witnesses are equal iff their underlying cycles are equal, equivalently iff their chains are equal.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.addBoundary
api.statement: For w∈C₄, replacing z by z+d₄w is a witness above the same β and has the same homology representative.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.choose
api.statement: If ψ is surjective, classical choice and the surjectivity of π provide a witness over every β. This API has no executable or functorial-choice guarantee.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.map
api.statement: A map of cycle modules compatible with ψπ maps witnesses over β to witnesses over the image of β; the maps induced by group/field maps are those from V.1.

api.name: BarLiftCertificate.map_id_comp
api.statement: Maps of witness fibres respect identity and composition.

tests.name: BarLiftCertificate_zero_test
tests.statement: The certificate of the zero cycle above 0 has zero chain and zero homology representative.

tests.name: BarLiftCertificate_boundary_test
tests.statement: For any c and four-chain w, the witness addBoundary(c,w) has the same image under Mathlib’s homology projection π as c.

tests.name: BarLiftCertificate_trivial_group
tests.statement: For the trivial group and any ψ:H₃(1,ℤ)→B, no witness exists over β≠0, because H₃(1,ℤ)=0.

tests.name: BarLiftCertificate_one_cube
tests.statement: For the trivial group, the single chain [1|1|1] with coefficient 1 is a cycle representing zero homology. It is a witness above 0 distinct as a finite chain from the zero witness. Thus equality of homology must not be used as extensionality of witnesses.

nodes.title: Good-prime finite-coefficient K₃ and étale Bloch identification
nodes.statement: Let F be a number field, p an odd prime, a≥1, n=p^a and p∤w₂(F). Use the imported finite-coefficient Quillen group K₃(F;ℤ/n), whose exact sequence is 0→K₃(F)/n --j_K→ K₃(F;ℤ/n) --∂_K→ K₂(F)[n]→0. Use the Habiro-owned CGZ étale Bloch group B_CGZ(F;ℤ/n), with its exact sequence 0→B_CGZ(F)/n --j_B→ B_CGZ(F;ℤ/n) --δ_B→K₂(F)[n]→0. The finite Chern isomorphism c̄₂,₁:K₃(F;ℤ/n)≅H¹(F,ℤ/n(2)) and the CGZ isomorphism R_ζ:B_CGZ(F;ℤ/n)≅H¹(F,ℤ/n(2)), transported through the same chosen twist/Kummer convention for a primitive n-th root ζ, give Φ_ζ=R_ζ⁻¹∘c̄₂,₁. In the additional range n prime to M_F of Habiro HB.1, write R_ζ∘κq=c_ζ^γ on K₃(F)/n using HB.2/the-comparison-with-the-chern-class. Then Φ_ζ∘j_K=j_B∘(γ⁻¹κq), with multiplicative powers interpreted as scalar multiplication on the additive target. No assertion δ_BΦ_ζ=∂_K is made without checking the right-hand normalization. In particular Φ is not asserted to extend the unscaled Suslin map.
hypotheses: F a number field; n=p^a, p odd, a≥1 and p∤w₂(F). These hypotheses imply F has no primitive p-th root of unity and put the two imported isomorphisms in their stated ranges.

c̄ uses the Soulé convention of M.8, and R_ζ uses the HB.2 twist convention. The equality on the modulo subgroup additionally uses n prime to M_F; γ is the unit from the existing HB comparison, without asserting a value here.
The finite Chern isomorphism for number fields without adjoining μ_n is requested from M.7: use Hutchinson Theorem 2.10 and K₃^M(F)/n=0, not the narrower corollary requiring μ_n⊂F.
proofSteps: Import finite-coefficient K-theory and its universal coefficient sequence through HB.1/finite-coefficient-K3-and-the-chern-class. Import the finite Chern class and its compatibility with j_K from M.8.

Obtain the degree-three finite Chern isomorphism from M.7, with the odd-prime Milnor quotient zero by V.2/milnor-k3-number-field. The source proof input is Hutchinson Theorem 2.10, not an application of Corollary 2.11 over the wrong field.
Import both the étale Bloch object and R_ζ isomorphism from HB.2/etale-bloch-group-and-K2. Use only its number-field good-prime statement. It is not rebuilt in V.6.
Compose the inverse of R_ζ with the finite Chern isomorphism. For the modulo restriction, HB.1/hutchinson-chern-class-agrees identifies c̄j_K with c_ζ, and HB.2’s γ comparison gives the factor γ⁻¹.
Keep the right-end Bockstein normalization as a recorded gap. The exact sequences already show why ordinary quotient comparison does not remove K₂(F)[n].

sources.locator: §2.3, Theorem 2.10 and the universal coefficient sequence, p4
sources.match: The finite Chern isomorphism is imported from its owning roadmap; the Milnor quotient vanishes at odd n for number fields.
Supplies the existing HB.2 good-prime isomorphism; composition gives Φ. Its source normalization must not be silently equated with the finite Chern class.

acceptance: The prototype named finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv takes two genuine additive equivalences into the same group H and has R(Φ(x))=c(x), with inverse c⁻¹R. This tests the construction without inventing missing K-theory/cohomology types.
The prototype named finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_on_quotient requires the actual commutative equations c j_K=h₀ and R j_B=γh₀ and yields the γ⁻¹ factor.
For F=ℚ,n=5, K₃(ℚ)/5=0, while HB.2’s class [32] has δ_B([32])={2,−31}≠0 with tame symbol 2 of order 5 at 31. Thus neither finite-coefficient middle group can be replaced by the ordinary quotient.
No arbitrary-field comparison or good-prime extension at 2 is exported.

uses.where: V.6’s finite-coefficient target and CGZ §6 equations (37)–(38)
uses.how: Constructs an identification of the actual finite-coefficient middle groups, using the two existing cohomology comparisons.
Its quotient-subgroup restriction remembers the inverse comparison scalar, rather than silently identifying it with the raw Suslin map.

api.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv
api.statement: For genuine additive equivalences c:K≃H and r:E≃H, the resulting Φ:K≃E is r⁻¹c. For the field specialization, c is the supplied finite Chern equivalence and r is the supplied R_ζ equivalence.

api.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_spec
api.statement: r(Φ(x))=c(x), and Φ⁻¹(y)=c⁻¹(r(y)). The first equation uniquely characterizes Φ.

api.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_def
api.statement: The generic construction is exactly Mathlib’s AddEquiv composition c.trans r.symm.

api.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_on_quotient
api.statement: For n-torsion modules L,H, a linear map h₀:L→H, a unit γ∈ℤ/n, and inclusions j_K:L→K,j_B:L→E satisfying c j_K=h₀ and r j_B=γh₀, one has Φ j_K(x)=j_B(γ⁻¹x). This is the field restriction after L=K₃(F)/n is identified with B_CGZ(F)/n.

api.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_natural
api.statement: Given supplied equivalences c′:K′≃H′,r′:E′≃H′ and homomorphisms f:K→K′,g:E→E′,h:H→H′ with c′f=hc and r′g=hr, one has Φ′f=gΦ. Field-extension naturality uses exactly these supplied commuting comparisons in their common good-prime range.

tests.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_mod_five
tests.statement: In K=E=H=ℤ/5, let c(x)=2x and r(x)=3x. Then Φ(1)=4. Reversing the equivalences gives the wrong answer.

tests.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_zero
tests.statement: For K=E=H=ℤ/1 and any supplied equivalences, Φ(0)=0.

tests.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_composition
tests.statement: For actual Mathlib additive equivalences c,r, Φ equals c.trans r.symm, including its inverse map c⁻¹r.

tests.name: finiteCoefficientBlochEquiv_middle_not_left
tests.statement: The exact sequence 0→0→ℤ/5→ℤ/5→0 has middle group not isomorphic to its left group: there is no additive equivalence ℤ/1≃ℤ/5. This tests the finite-coefficient K₂-term distinction in a finite model; the arithmetic acceptance instance is F=ℚ,n=5 and [32].

requests.need: For every number field F, odd p and a≥1, the degree-three finite Chern comparison identifies K₃(F;ℤ/p^a) with H¹(F,ℤ/p^a(2)). Export the exact finite-coefficient indecomposable quotient used by Hutchinson Theorem 2.10 and the reduction to the full group when K₃^M(F)/p^a=0. Do not require μ_{p^a}⊂F.

Export Soulé’s finite c̄₂,₁ with its compatibility along j_K:K₃(F)/n→K₃(F;ℤ/n), the p-adic-to-finite reduction, and the ζ twist/Kummer convention used in HB.1/hutchinson-chern-class-agrees. Also identify the induced map on the K₂[n] Bockstein term, with its scalar/sign, for comparison to CGZ δ_B.

remaining: Produce an effective certificate-to-Steinberg-bar-cycle construction, beyond the explicitly noncomputable witness selection.
Supply the requested M.7 finite Chern isomorphism and M.8 reduction/twist/Bockstein compatibility; verify the right-end scalar of Φ.

gaps.title: Effective five-term certificate to finite Steinberg bar cycle
gaps.detail: The parent proves existential surjectivity and this part provides finite-chain witnesses and a classical choose API. Neither the read VI.5.12 proof nor the circular-unit remark gives an executable procedure which takes a finite boundary/equality certificate and outputs z∈C₃(St(F),ℤ), a checked d₃z=0 and ψπz=β. Establish and source the chain-level lifting construction with its auxiliary choices and termination/range hypotheses; do not describe classical choose as the requested algorithm.

gaps.title: Right-end normalization of the finite-coefficient comparison
gaps.detail: The two good-prime isomorphisms yield Φ=R_ζ⁻¹c̄ and determine its scaled restriction to K₃/n in the M_F range. Identify the map δ_BΦ on K₂(F)[n] against the K-theory Bockstein ∂_K and Tate’s degree-two Chern map in the exact convention. CGZ equation (38) by itself is not a license to set the scalar to 1 after importing the separately normalized Soulé map. The required degree-two compatibility is requested from M.8.

gaps.title: Inherited degree-three Hurewicz input for the stable Steinberg model
gaps.detail: V.1/k3-h3-steinberg imports the absolute Hurewicz theorem π₃(X)≅H₃(X,ℤ) for the 2-connected space BSt(F)⁺ and the bar-versus-singular homology comparison for BSt(F). Its reviewed parent records an upstream-citation gap for the Hurewicz input. This part uses the exact imported statement and retains that gap; it neither closes the upstream citation nor replaces the stable Steinberg group by the elementary group. Resolve that inherited proof input in the V.1 owner before claiming the witness construction closed.

restructure.detail: RT-AREA-ktheory-2/23: V.6’s final regulator sentence duplicates P.2 and D.2. The follow-up document deletes that target from V.6. It also refines, rather than replaces, the parent’s bundled root-of-unity-class.
restructure.proposal: V.6 owns algebraic elements, certificates, root substitutes and the comparisons stated here. P.2 owns the real agreement, checked against BorelRegulators:R.7; D.2 owns the p-adic agreement (D.3 is not its supplier). The rational and integral Suslin maps needed for those analytic comparisons are already provided by K3BlochGroups:V.4 and can be imported directly there. Do not introduce a whole-stage V.6→P.2 or V.6→D.2 dependency through the finite-coefficient node: this part consumes M.8, which in turn depends on P/D inputs. If an analytic owner needs a V.6-specific certificate interface, split that algebraic substage before adding the corresponding outgoing edge. At assembly retain the parent’s two planets (five-term-certificate and bloch-element-constructor) and the four new root/lift planets: the combined layer then has exactly six. No original packet, campaign text or atlas data is edited in this job.

restructure.detail: The source-level order is algebraic V.6 comparisons → HB.2’s étale Bloch theorem → the new finite-coefficient identification. Collapsing this to whole-stage arrows would produce a V.6/HB.2 cycle.
restructure.proposal: Propose V.6a, Algebraic elements and certificates, containing the retained parent V.6 algebraic/certificate nodes and the four new root/lift nodes; propose V.6b, Arithmetic finite-coefficient identification, containing finite-coefficient-identification. Retain all node ids at assembly. The input directions are V.6a→HabiroNumberFields:HB.2→V.6b and MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.7/M.8→V.6b. Any V.6-specific certificate exports to P.2/D.2 come only from V.6a. This proposal leaves the current exact issue scope V.6 unchanged while making the acyclic supplier/consumer split explicit.
